title: Java Interoperability Fundamentals knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the main idea of “Java Interoperability Fundamentals”?
options: It removes the need to understand types or runtime behavior.
Kotlin and Java interoperate, but platform types, annotations, generated JVM signatures, and collection mutability require explicit boundary checks.
It makes versioning, input validation, and testing unnecessary.
It means all Kotlin libraries and platform APIs behave identically.
questions.answer_key: Kotlin and Java interoperate, but platform types, annotations, generated JVM signatures, and collection mutability require explicit boundary checks.
questions.explanation: The reliable answer is grounded in the lesson’s main principle: Kotlin and Java interoperate, but platform types, annotations, generated JVM signatures, and collection mutability require explicit boundary checks. questions.answer_key: Use a minimal reproducible example, compare the actual result with the expected result, and check the target/version assumptions.
